Subject: Questions on default retention for request/response logs

Hi Neha —

Thanks for the demo earlier. FinTech Co. legal/security team has a few follow-ups so we can complete our vendor review. Can you confirm Redwood's default retention behavior for hosted API logs? Specifically:

- For request and response bodies (prompts and generated outputs), what is the default retention period?
- Are prompts and outputs stored together or are they separated into different retention buckets (e.g., prompt text vs. generated token stream)?
- How are logs / request metadata partitioned by region? If we pick EU region, will the request/response data be stored only in EU data centers?
- What are the deletion options? Can we auto-expire after X days, or request immediate purge? How long does a purge take and is there an audit trail?

I've attached a short spreadsheet that lists our policy thresholds (retention windows, legal holds, etc.). Please loop in security and product if useful.

Thanks for the clear list. Looping in Vivek (security), Grace (product), and Markus (legal) to provide definitive answers and a concise export we can attach to your assessment. High-level answers below; we will follow up with a one‑pager and the DPA excerpt.

High-level (hosted API):
- Default retention: request/response bodies (including prompts and outputs) are retained for 30 days by default.
- Prompts and outputs: stored together as request content; they follow the same default retention policy.
- Region: when you select an EU region for the account, request/response content is stored in EU data centers by default.
- Deletion: customers can set a shorter retention policy (e.g., 7/14/30 days) via account settings for hosted accounts. For immediate purges, we can perform an on-demand deletion (support ticket) which includes an audit record. Details below from Vivek.

Attaching the one‑pager with sample language you can include in your vendor assessment. If anything in the attached sheet requires different wording for procurement/legal, Markus will advise.

Next steps: Vivek will add technical detail (log tiers, audit trails), Markus will confirm DPA redlines, and Grace will note Dedicated/Private differences.

Subject: Re: Questions on default retention for request/response logs

Hi Carlos / team —

Thanks for the questions. Below are the technical clarifications to supplement Neha's summary. I kept this intentionally concrete so you can paste into your security questionnaire.

1) Default retention windows (hosted API)
- Request/response content (prompts + generated outputs): 30 days by default. This is the \"request content\" bucket.
- System audit logs (platform events, access logs): retained for 365 days by default; can be shortened for customers under contract.
- Aggregated telemetry/usage metrics (token counts, latency): retained for analytics purposes (12 months) and are pseudonymized; they do not contain plaintext prompts/outputs.

2) Storage and separation
- Prompts and outputs are persisted together as the request payload for retrieval and debugging; they are not stored in a separate retention bucket by default.
- We do maintain a separate metadata index (request id, timestamp, model version, region) that is retained under the audit/system retention policy above.

3) Region and residency guarantees
- For hosted accounts configured in an EU region, request content is written to EU-only storage endpoints. Replication to other regions does not occur unless you enable cross-region failover or use multi-region routing.
- Logs used for platform operations (internal monitoring, aggregated metrics) are subject to strict access controls and are either region-limited or pseudonymized depending on the dataset.

4) Deletion and retention controls
- Self-service retention policy: account admins can set a retention TTL (7/14/30/90 days) for request content via Console -> Data controls.
- On-demand purge: we can accept a support request to purge data immediately for a given time range or request id set. Typical turnaround for hosted API requests is 24–72 hours; upon completion we provide an audit record (timestamp, operator id, affected record count).
- Compliance hold: if you need legal hold, we can freeze deletion for subject IDs and provide export capabilities for the retained set. Holds are handled through our legal operations workflow.

5) Dedicated / Private differences
- Dedicated: retention defaults can be contractually set; you can request shorter/longer windows at provisioning time. Data remains in the region specified for the Dedicated capacity.
- Private (VPC/on‑prem): you control retention because the storage is under your network and/or customer-managed buckets; Redwood's control plane can be configured to not persist request content if desired.

6) Use of customer data for model training
- By default, Redwood does not use customer prompts/outputs for model training unless explicitly opted into via contract. This is documented in the DPA.

If helpful, I can provide example Console screenshots and the API call we use for on‑demand purge (we'll redact internal operator ids from the sample).

—Vivek
Head of Security, Redwood Inference
